source.extractionPreview:
The rich diversity of chemical behaviour of different 
elements can be traced to the differences in the internal 
structure of atoms of these elements.

structure of atom

their characteristics;

describe Thomson, Rutherford
and Bohr atomic models;
•

of the quantum mechanical model
of atom;

activities.subject: Chemistry
activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 2.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.
activities.sourceTextSummary: Generated from Chemistry  - Part 1, Chapter Chapter 2.

correctItems.text: The rich diversity of chemical behaviour of different elements can be traced to the differences in the internal structure of atoms of these elements.
The existence of atoms has been proposed since the time of early Indian and Greek philosophers (400 B.C.) who were of the view that atoms are the fundamental building blocks of matter.
According to them, the continued subdivisions of matter would ultimately yield atoms which would not be further divisible.
The word 'atom' has been derived from the Greek word 'a-tomio' which means 'uncut-able' or 'non-divisible'.

correctItems.text: Dalton's atomic theory was able to explain the law of conservation of mass, law of constant composition and law of multiple proportion very successfully.
However, it failed to explain the results of many experiments, for example, it was known that substances like glass or ebonite when rubbed with silk or fur get electrically charged.
In this unit we start with the experimental observations made by scientists towards the end of nineteenth and beginning of twentieth century.
These established that atoms are made of sub-atomic particles, i.e., electrons, protons and neutrons - a concept very different from that of Dalton.

activities.modelAnswer: The rich diversity of chemical behaviour of different elements can be traced to the differences in the internal structure of atoms of these elements. The existence of atoms has been proposed since the time of early Indian and Greek philosophers (400 B.C.) who were of the view that atoms are the fundamental building blocks of matter. According to them, the continued subdivisions of matter would ultimately yield atoms which would not be further divisible. The word 'atom' has been derived from the Greek word 'a-tomio' which means 'uncut-able' or 'non-divisible'.
